title: Centering the Margins: Outlier-Based Identification of Harmed Populations in Toxicity Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of toxicity classifiers between demographic outliers and non-outliers based on racial group annotations (e.g., Black, Latine, Asian) in the Jigsaw Unintended Bias dataset.

Comparing the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of toxicity classifiers between demographic outliers and non-outliers based on gender annotations (e.g., women, 'other gender identity') in the Jigsaw Unintended Bias dataset.

Comparing the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of toxicity classifiers between demographic outliers and non-outliers based on sexual orientation annotations (e.g., gay, lesbian, bisexual) in the Jigsaw Unintended Bias dataset.

Comparing the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of toxicity classifiers between demographic outliers and non-outliers based on religious minority annotations (e.g., atheist, Buddhist, Hindu, Jewish, Muslim) in the Jigsaw Unintended Bias dataset.

Comparing the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of toxicity classifiers between demographic outliers and non-outliers based on disability annotations (e.g., intellectual, physical, psychiatric) in the Jigsaw Unintended Bias dataset.

Employing the Local Outlier Factor (LOF) algorithm to identify text and demographic outliers across multiple intersecting identity categories simultaneously, and measuring the toxicity prediction error (MSE) disparities for these marginalized subgroups.
